agent_authored.description: CLASS (Cosmic Linear Anisotropy Solving System) is a C-based cosmological Boltzmann solver. It evolves the homogeneous background, recombination and thermodynamics, perturbation hierarchy, primordial spectra, transfer functions, harmonic spectra, lensing and optional Fourier/non-linear observables for cosmological inference and theory scans.

modules.title: CLASS cosmological background, perturbation, transfer and spectrum solver
modules.expensive_path: The perturbation hierarchy and subsequent transfer, harmonic and Fourier integrations evolve many k modes and source functions; the work scales with precision, multipole cutoffs, k sampling and requested spectra and is the principal path whose acceleration would shorten cosmological inference and theory scans.
modules.rationale: CLASS is a unified production solver: background, thermodynamics, perturbations, primordial spectra, transfer functions and output spectra share the same numerical state and are exercised through the command-line and wrapper entry points.  The latest pipeline guidance defaults to one whole-codebase module when the physics is not independently separable; this cut preserves the scientific dependency graph and allows checks to select distinct official stages without pretending they are standalone codebases.
excluded: doc/ and the committed PDF/manual assets are documentation, not runnable production physics.
notebooks/ and external/RealSpaceInterface are auxiliary analysis/UI material rather than the core CLASS solver path.
output/ reference tables and external numerical data are inputs or generated artifacts; they are retained only where an official example needs them.

test/test_thermodynamics.c is excluded from the first survey as an upstream compile incompatibility at the pinned commit (removed index_th_tau_d member); it should be revisited after upstream clarification.
hazards: The upstream repository has no SPDX license file; README permission and citation language require maintainer confirmation before vendoring.

Floating-point summation order, compiler flags, OpenMP scheduling and adaptive integration can move printed spectra; output columns and tolerances must be calibrated from the source and a Linux build.
The Python wrapper and some external modules add dependencies (NumPy, SciPy, Cython, pandas, matplotlib, pynose and parameterized) beyond the minimal C binary.
The official thermodynamics C test does not compile at the pinned commit and must be documented rather than hidden.
